title: Follow-up: harden the GCLI-14 diff-path tests and the unquote fallback
description: Nits 1-3 of the DEC-183 APPROVE review of opum-ai/glyph-cli#62 (GCLI-14), recorded verbatim on GCLI-14. (1) test/cli.test.ts:118 exercises only a non-ASCII name, which a global core.quotePath=false renders raw, so it would pass with the fix reverted; makeScratchRepo sets only user.email and user.name and gitRun inherits {...process.env}. Pin core.quotePath=true in test/helpers.ts (or GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null in tests) so the CLI test is a real control. (2) unquoteGitPath is exported but has no direct literal-string test: a path containing a double quote, the named escapes beyond \t and \\, and both fall-back returns (an unknown escape, a trailing lone backslash) are untested. (3) new TextDecoder() is non-fatal, so a non-UTF-8 byte sequence becomes U+FFFD silently, which the docstring says the function avoids: use {fatal: true} and return the path unchanged on failure.

acceptanceCriteria.text: test/helpers.ts pins core.quotePath=true (or the tests run with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null), so a caller config with quotePath=false cannot make the CLI test pass.
A direct literal-string test of unquoteGitPath covers a double quote, the named escapes beyond \t and \\, an unknown escape and a trailing lone backslash; it depends on no git config.
unquoteGitPath decodes with a fatal UTF-8 decoder and returns the input path unchanged on a non-UTF-8 sequence, with a test for that path.
bun run check passes and removing the unquoting still turns the CLI test red under the pinned config.
